title: LUNAR Lab presents at EMNLP 2024
description:
Members of the LUNAR Lab will be presenting two papers and a workshop contribution at the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), held in Miami, Florida.

The first paper, "Probing Syntactic Representations Across Transformer Depth," presents a systematic probing study of how syntactic information — including constituency, dependency structure, and binding relations — is distributed across the layers of transformer-based language models. We find that syntactic representations peak at intermediate depths and are more robust than previously reported when evaluated under controlled lexical conditions.

The second paper, "When Does Context Help? A Pragmatic Analysis of In-Context Learning," investigates the conditions under which providing examples in the prompt reliably improves model performance. We propose a pragmatic framing of in-context learning and show that models are sensitive to the informativeness and coherence of demonstrations in ways that parallel human pragmatic reasoning.

Additionally, lab member Sarah Okonkwo will present a position paper at the BlackboxNLP workshop on the limits of probing as a tool for mechanistic interpretability.

If you are attending EMNLP this year, we would love to connect. Find us at our paper sessions or reach out in advance to arrange a meeting.
